So, can anyone think of a reason why we aren't on solar, wind, and alternatives like these? The alternatives I'm thinking of don't require incredible regulation and have little environmental cost in comparison. I can only come up with one thing - profit. And it's not even "legit" profit (as if in economic benefit to society). It's profit based on a bad valuation because we don't capture the costs of externalities. Let me explain my POV:

Society faces the following trade-off: Environmental and other costs for using some special power source (nuclear or oil) vs (incremental benefit of using a safer method minus cost of implementing new method). I believe the number on the left is large and negative while the number on the right is medium and positive. What could explain society picking the higher-cost option (keeping the large environmental costs)? Well, there's more profit for shareholders in the thing on the right since they won't get charged for the costs on the left. Does this matter? Well, are the one's deciding the matter for society shareholders or society at large? Oops, (shareholders). Our wrong valuation (not properly returning the cost to negative externalities back to the offenders) has made shareholders and elites choose something admittedly rational for them, but bad for society.

Often in can come down to location as well. If you place massive windmills in a huge wind farm it could disrupt the local ecosystem which obviously impacts the larger system as well. I know one of the issues with the cape cod farm was that some activist groups were concerned it was going to harm local fish and whale life.

Obviously a lot has to do with big oil not wanting it to cut into their profits but at the same time there are a lot of issues with setting up the infrastructure. Not proposing it can't be done but that it has to be done carefully.

  • People are nice and like to actually converse.
